_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 05:11:58Z)**_

Issue #71 is **"Add Toggle to Switch Between Text-Field and Calendar Grid Modes"**, a sub-issue of #32. Dylan Han opened it, it's assigned to you, and it's labeled `enhancement` and `effort:medium`. There are no comments yet.

**The problem:** Once the new visual availability grid exists, users need a way to switch between it and the current text-field input. Both should stay available so people who prefer typing aren't pushed onto the new UI.

**What it asks for:**
- A clearly labeled toggle on the **availability settings page**, such as a segmented button reading **"Text" / "Visual"**.
- Clicking it switches which input mode is shown. **Only one mode is visible at a time.**
- The chosen mode **stays the same for the rest of the session**, but doesn't need to be saved permanently.

**What's out of scope:**
- **Keeping data in sync between the two modes is not part of this issue.** Issue #72 makes switching lossless. #71 only controls which mode is visible.
- **The existing text-field UI must stay completely unchanged.**
- The issue rules out showing both modes side by side, and asking users to pick a default once during onboarding.

**Dependency:** It needs **#69** (the grid component) to exist first, since there's nothing to toggle to without it.

Do you want me to check whether #69 has been merged, and find the availability settings page code where the toggle would go?

```text
Build the Weekly Availability Grid Component
CLOSED
### Summary
Create a new React component that renders a weekly grid with days of the week on the X-axis and hours (midnight to 11:59 PM) on the Y-axis. This serves as the foundational visual element for the drag-to-select availability feature.

### User story
As an event host, I want to see my weekly availability displayed across days and hours on an intuitive grid, so that I can clearly review my recurring open time slots.

### Rough scope
Medium — requires creating a responsive React grid component (7 days × 24 hourly rows), rendering time and day labels, implementing selected/unselected visual states driven by props, and embedding the component into the availability settings page layout. (Excludes drag interactions, data mutation, and backend/DB persistence).

### Source
Feature enhancement for availability configuration and foundational prerequisite for the drag-to-select scheduling interface.

### Describe the solution you'd like
Build and style the core weekly calendar grid component according to the following specifications:

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Grid displays 7 columns (days of the week: Sun–Sat) and 24 rows (hourly slots: 12:00 AM–11:00 PM).
- Time labels are rendered along the Y-axis.
- Day labels are rendered along the X-axis.
- Grid cells support distinct visual styles for "selected" and "unselected" states. 
- Component accepts availability state as a prop and renders the matching cell states accordingly.
- Component is fully responsive and integrates cleanly into the existing availability settings page layout.

**Out of scope:**
- Drag-and-drop / drag-to-select interactions.
- Data synchronization and API/DB persistence.

---

## Requirements Specification

## User Story
As a Cal.diy user, I want a visual weekly grid showing days and hours so that I have a spatial representation of my availability to interact with and so it is easier to input my availability.

## User Scenario
A user navigates to the availability settings page. Instead of seeing only text boxes, they see a 7-column, 24-row grid (exact numbers can be adjusted) with day labels across the top and hour labels down the left side. Cells that correspond to currently set available hours appear highlighted. The user can see their whole week's availability at a glance without reading any text fields.

Ultimately (the ideal implementation after the full completion of Issue #32), the user clicks and drags on the calendar to modify his availability. When the user toggles between calendar and text field mode, the user sees the same information.

## Acceptance Criteria
For now:
1. Grid renders 7 columns (Sun–Sat) with day labels on the X-axis
2. Grid renders 24 rows with hour labels (12:00 AM, 1:00 AM, … 11:00 PM) on the Y-axis
3. Cells have visually distinct "selected" and "unselected" states (e.g. filled vs. unfilled color); "distinct" may be hard to exactly specify, so let's say that the color and shading must be different between selected and unselected cells

## Out of Scope
- Drag-to-select interaction (Issue #70)
- Toggle between grid and text-field modes (Issue #71)
- Syncing grid state with text fields (Issue #73)
- Database reads/writes (Issue #73)

## Open Questions
- Should the Y-axis start at midnight or at a configurable earliest hour (e.g. 6:00 AM) to reduce whitespace?
- Should the appearance change based on the system settings (e.g. light vs dark mode)?
- How should the appearance change based on the size of the screen (e.g. phone vs computer)?
```

Both #69 and the codebase are ready, and most of the groundwork for #71 is already there.

## Issue #69 status
- **#69 was merged in PR #84** (Oct 8), and your branch `feat/issue-71` contains it. Your branch is level with `team/main`.
- **The drag editing from #70 is also merged** (PR #90).
- **The grid's unit tests pass.** I ran the three test files for the component, its helpers and the drag hook: 73/73 passed. I didn't run the full type-check.

## What already exists for #71

1. **The switch is already built, but nothing uses it.** `AvailabilitySettings` in `packages/platform/atoms/availability/AvailabilitySettings.tsx` has an `availabilityView?: "list" | "grid"` prop, defaulting to `"list"`. Around line 716 it renders either the grid or the existing text-field `<Schedule>`, never both, which is exactly what the issue asks for. But the availability page (`apps/web/modules/availability/[schedule]/schedule-view.tsx`) never passes the prop, so **users can't reach the grid today.** Your task is mainly to add a control that drives this switch.

2. **Switching modes already keeps the data.** The grid writes to the same `schedule` form field the text fields use, so edits in one mode show up in the other and Save handles both. That means #72 (state sync) is largely done already. It's worth telling your team so nobody duplicates it.

3. **The text-field UI won't need any changes.** The toggle only chooses which mode to render, so it meets the "existing UI must remain unmodified" requirement.

4. **The pieces for the control already exist:**
   - There's a segmented button component at `packages/ui/components/form/toggleGroup/ToggleGroup.tsx`, already used in `bookings-people-view.tsx`. Import it from the direct path rather than the barrel file, per the repo rules.
   - The translation key `"text": "Text"` already exists. You'd only need to add a `"visual"` key to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.

## Decisions before coding
- **Where the toggle's state lives.** I recommend keeping it inside `AvailabilitySettings`, using the existing prop as the starting value. That keeps the change in one place and still works for the other caller (`AvailabilitySettingsPlatformWrapper`).
- **How "persists within the session" works.** Plain React state resets when you leave the page. To keep the choice across pages, save it in `sessionStorage`, with a fallback to text mode if storage isn't available.

Together that's roughly one or two files plus a translation key, well within the PR size limits.

```text
import * as RadixToggleGroup from "@radix-ui/react-toggle-group";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { useState } from "react";

import classNames from "@calcom/ui/classNames";

import { Tooltip } from "../../tooltip/Tooltip";

interface ToggleGroupProps extends Omit<RadixToggleGroup.ToggleGroupSingleProps, "type"> {
  options: {
    value: string;
    label: string | ReactNode;
    disabled?: boolean;
    tooltip?: string;
    iconLeft?: ReactNode;
    dataTestId?: string;
    onClick?: VoidFunction;
  }[];
  isFullWidth?: boolean;
  orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical";
}

const OptionalTooltipWrapper = ({
  children,
  tooltipText,
}: {
  children: ReactNode;
  tooltipText?: ReactNode;
}) => {
  if (tooltipText) {
    return (
      <Tooltip delayDuration={150} sideOffset={12} side="bottom" content={tooltipText}>
        {children}
      </Tooltip>
    );
  }
  return <>{children}</>;
};

export const ToggleGroup = ({
  options,
  onValueChange,
  isFullWidth,
  orientation = "horizontal",
  customClassNames,
  defaultValue,
  ...props
}: ToggleGroupProps & { customClassNames?: string }) => {
  const isControlled = props.value !== undefined;
  const [uncontrolledValue, setUncontrolledValue] = useState(defaultValue ?? "");

  return (
    <>
      <RadixToggleGroup.Root
        type="single"
        {...props}
        {...(isControlled ? { value: props.value } : { value: uncontrolledValue })}
        orientation={orientation}
        onValueChange={(value) => {
          if (!value) return;
          if (!isControlled) {
            setUncontrolledValue(value);
          }
          onValueChange?.(value);
        }}
        style={{
          // @ts-expect-error --toggle-group-shadow is not a valid CSS property but can be a variable
          "--toggle-group-shadow":
            "0px 2px 3px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.03), 0px 2px 2px -1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.03)",
        }}
        className={classNames(
          `bg-muted rounded-[10px] p-0.5`,
          orientation === "horizontal" && "inline-flex gap-0.5 rtl:flex-row-reverse",
          orientation === "vertical" && "flex w-fit flex-col gap-0.5",
          props.className,
          isFullWidth && "w-full",
          customClassNames
        )}>
        {options.map((option) => (
          <OptionalTooltipWrapper key={option.value} tooltipText={option.tooltip}>
            <RadixToggleGroup.Item
              disabled={option.disabled}
              onClick={option?.onClick}
              value={option.value}
              data-testid={option.dataTestId ?? `toggle-group-item-${option.value}`}
              className={classNames(
                "aria-checked:bg-default aria-checked:border-subtle rounded-lg border border-transparent p-1.5 text-sm leading-none transition aria-checked:shadow-[0px_2px_3px_0px_rgba(0,0,0,0.03),0px_2px_2px_-1px_rgba(0,0,0,0.03)]",
                option.disabled
                  ? "text-gray-400 hover:cursor-not-allowed"
                  : "text-default [&[aria-checked='false']]:hover:text-emphasis [&[aria-checked='false']]:hover:bg-subtle cursor-pointer",
                isFullWidth && "w-full"
              )}>
              <div
                className={classNames(
                  "flex items-center gap-1",
                  orientation === "horizontal" && "justify-center",
                  orientation === "vertical" && "justify-start"
                )}>
                {option.iconLeft && <span className="flex h-4 w-4 items-center">{option.iconLeft}</span>}
                {option.label}
              </div>
            </RadixToggleGroup.Item>
          </OptionalTooltipWrapper>
        ))}
      </RadixToggleGroup.Root>
    </>
  );
};
```

```text
/**
 * Provides a wrapper around localStorage and sessionStorage to avoid errors in case of restricted storage access.
 *
 * TODO: In case of an embed if localStorage is not available(third party), use localStorage of parent(first party) that contains the iframe.
 */
export const localStorage = {
  getItem(key: string) {
    try {
      return window.localStorage.getItem(key);
    } catch {
      // In case storage is restricted. Possible reasons
      // 1. Third Party Context in Chrome Incognito mode.
      return null;
    }
  },
  setItem(key: string, value: string) {
    try {
      window.localStorage.setItem(key, value);
    } catch {
      // In case storage is restricted. Possible reasons
      // 1. Third Party Context in Chrome Incognito mode.
      // 2. Storage limit reached
      return;
    }
  },
  removeItem: (key: string) => {
    try {
      window.localStorage.removeItem(key);
    } catch {
      return;
    }
  },
};

export const sessionStorage = {
  getItem(key: string) {
    try {
      // eslint-disable-next-line @calcom/eslint/avoid-web-storage
      return window.sessionStorage.getItem(key);
    } catch {
      // In case storage is restricted. Possible reasons
      // 1. Third Party Context in Chrome Incognito mode.
      return null;
    }
  },
  setItem(key: string, value: string) {
    try {
      // eslint-disable-next-line @calcom/eslint/avoid-web-storage
      window.sessionStorage.setItem(key, value);
    } catch {
      // In case storage is restricted. Possible reasons
      // 1. Third Party Context in Chrome Incognito mode.
      // 2. Storage limit reached
      return;
    }
  },
  removeItem: (key: string) => {
    try {
      // eslint-disable-next-line @calcom/eslint/avoid-web-storage
      window.sessionStorage.removeItem(key);
    } catch {
      return;
    }
  },
};
```

```typescript
import { sessionStorage } from "@calcom/lib/webstorage";
import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from "react";

export type AvailabilityView = "list" | "grid";

export const AVAILABILITY_VIEW_STORAGE_KEY = "availability-view";

export const isAvailabilityView = (value: string): value is AvailabilityView =>
  value === "list" || value === "grid";

export function useAvailabilityView() {
  // Always start as "list" so the server render and first client render match; the stored
  // choice is applied after mount to avoid a hydration mismatch
  const [view, setView] = useState<AvailabilityView>("list");

  useEffect(() => {
    const storedView = sessionStorage.getItem(AVAILABILITY_VIEW_STORAGE_KEY);
    if (storedView && isAvailabilityView(storedView)) setView(storedView);
  }, []);

  const updateView = useCallback((nextView: AvailabilityView) => {
    setView(nextView);
    sessionStorage.setItem(AVAILABILITY_VIEW_STORAGE_KEY, nextView);
  }, []);

  return [view, updateView] as const;
}

```

```typescript
import { useLocale } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale";
import { ToggleGroup } from "@calcom/ui/components/form";
import type { AvailabilityView } from "../hooks/useAvailabilityView";
import { isAvailabilityView } from "../hooks/useAvailabilityView";

type AvailabilityViewToggleProps = {
  value: AvailabilityView;
  onValueChange: (view: AvailabilityView) => void;
};

export function AvailabilityViewToggle({ value, onValueChange }: AvailabilityViewToggleProps) {
  const { t } = useLocale();

  return (
    <ToggleGroup
      aria-label={t("availability_input_mode")}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={(nextView) => {
        if (isAvailabilityView(nextView)) onValueChange(nextView);
      }}
      options={[
        { value: "list", label: t("text"), dataTestId: "availability-view-text" },
        { value: "grid", label: t("visual"), dataTestId: "availability-view-visual" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

```typescript
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { AvailabilityViewToggle } from "./AvailabilityViewToggle";

const textOption = () => screen.getByTestId("availability-view-text");
const visualOption = () => screen.getByTestId("availability-view-visual");

describe("AvailabilityViewToggle", () => {
  it("renders a labelled group with Text and Visual options", () => {
    render(<AvailabilityViewToggle value="list" onValueChange={vi.fn()} />);

    expect(screen.getByRole("group")).toHaveAttribute("aria-label", "availability_input_mode");
    expect(textOption()).toHaveTextContent("text");
    expect(visualOption()).toHaveTextContent("visual");
  });

  it("marks only the current view as selected", () => {
    const { rerender } = render(<AvailabilityViewToggle value="list" onValueChange={vi.fn()} />);

    expect(textOption()).toHaveAttribute("aria-checked", "true");
    expect(visualOption()).toHaveAttribute("aria-checked", "false");

    rerender(<AvailabilityViewToggle value="grid" onValueChange={vi.fn()} />);

    expect(textOption()).toHaveAttribute("aria-checked", "false");
    expect(visualOption()).toHaveAttribute("aria-checked", "true");
  });

  it("reports the newly selected view on click", async () => {
    const onValueChange = vi.fn();
    render(<AvailabilityViewToggle value="list" onValueChange={onValueChange} />);

    await userEvent.click(visualOption());

    expect(onValueChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith("grid");
  });

  it("does not deselect the current view when it is clicked again", async () => {
    const onValueChange = vi.fn();
    render(<AvailabilityViewToggle value="list" onValueChange={onValueChange} />);

    await userEvent.click(textOption());

    expect(onValueChange).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("supports keyboard navigation with Tab, arrow keys and Space", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const onValueChange = vi.fn();
    render(<AvailabilityViewToggle value="list" onValueChange={onValueChange} />);

    await user.tab();
    expect(textOption()).toHaveFocus();

    await user.keyboard("{ArrowRight}");
    expect(visualOption()).toHaveFocus();

    await user.keyboard(" ");
    expect(onValueChange).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith("grid");
  });
});

```

```typescript
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { renderToString } from "react-dom/server";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { AvailabilityViewToggle } from "../components/AvailabilityViewToggle";
import { AVAILABILITY_VIEW_STORAGE_KEY, useAvailabilityView } from "./useAvailabilityView";

// Mirrors how the availability settings page wires the hook to the toggle and picks one view
function AvailabilityViewHarness() {
  const [view, setView] = useAvailabilityView();

  return (
    <>
      <AvailabilityViewToggle value={view} onValueChange={setView} />
      {view === "grid" ? <div data-testid="grid-view" /> : <div data-testid="list-view" />}
    </>
  );
}

const visualOption = () => screen.getByTestId("availability-view-visual");
const textOption = () => screen.getByTestId("availability-view-text");

describe("useAvailabilityView", () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    window.sessionStorage.clear();
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
  });

  it("defaults to the text view and shows only one view", () => {
    render(<AvailabilityViewHarness />);

    expect(screen.getByTestId("list-view")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("grid-view")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("switches between views, showing only one at a time", async () => {
    render(<AvailabilityViewHarness />);

    await userEvent.click(visualOption());
    expect(screen.getByTestId("grid-view")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("list-view")).not.toBeInTheDocument();

    await userEvent.click(textOption());
    expect(screen.getByTestId("list-view")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("grid-view")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("persists the selected view to sessionStorage", async () => {
    render(<AvailabilityViewHarness />);

    await userEvent.click(visualOption());

    expect(window.sessionStorage.getItem(AVAILABILITY_VIEW_STORAGE_KEY)).toBe("grid");
  });

  it("restores the stored view after remounting within the same session", async () => {
    const { unmount } = render(<AvailabilityViewHarness />);
    await userEvent.click(visualOption());
    unmount();

    render(<AvailabilityViewHarness />);

    expect(await screen.findByTestId("grid-view")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(visualOption()).toHaveAttribute("aria-checked", "true");
  });

  it("renders the text view on the server even when a visual view is stored", () => {
    window.sessionStorage.setItem(AVAILABILITY_VIEW_STORAGE_KEY, "grid");

    const html = renderToString(<AvailabilityViewHarness />);

    expect(html).toContain('data-testid="list-view"');
    expect(html).not.toContain('data-testid="grid-view"');
  });

  it("ignores unrecognised stored values", () => {
    window.sessionStorage.setItem(AVAILABILITY_VIEW_STORAGE_KEY, "calendar");

    render(<AvailabilityViewHarness />);

    expect(screen.getByTestId("list-view")).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("falls back to the text view when sessionStorage is unavailable", async () => {
    vi.spyOn(Storage.prototype, "getItem").mockImplementation(() => {
      throw new Error("SecurityError");
    });
    vi.spyOn(Storage.prototype, "setItem").mockImplementation(() => {
      throw new Error("SecurityError");
    });

    render(<AvailabilityViewHarness />);
    expect(screen.getByTestId("list-view")).toBeInTheDocument();

    await userEvent.click(visualOption());
    expect(screen.getByTestId("grid-view")).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

```

I've built the Text / Visual toggle on the availability settings page. Its tests pass, `apps/web` type-checks with no errors, and nothing is committed. The full `yarn type-check:ci --force` run did **not** pass, but the failures come from this Windows setup, not the code (details under Checks).

## Files changed

**New files (in `packages/features/schedules/`):**

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `hooks/useAvailabilityView.ts` | Holds the selected mode (`"list"` or `"grid"`) and saves it to `sessionStorage` using the repo's existing safe wrapper (`@calcom/lib/webstorage`), so a blocked or private-mode browser just falls back to Text. It always starts as `"list"` and applies the saved choice right after the page loads, so the server render and the browser render match. |
| `components/AvailabilityViewToggle.tsx` | Text / Visual segmented control built on the existing `ToggleGroup`. It gets an `aria-label`, keyboard support (Tab, arrow keys, Space/Enter) and a selected state from the underlying component, and clicking the already-selected option does nothing. |
| `components/AvailabilityViewToggle.test.tsx` | 5 tests: labels, only the current mode shown as selected, clicking to switch, re-clicking doesn't deselect, keyboard navigation. |
| `hooks/useAvailabilityView.test.tsx` | 7 tests: defaults to Text, switching shows one view at a time, choice saved to `sessionStorage`, choice restored after reloading the component, server render always shows Text, invalid saved values ignored, works when storage throws. |

**Modified files (+17 / −1):**
- **`packages/platform/atoms/availability/AvailabilitySettings.tsx`** (+11/−1): adds one optional prop, `onAvailabilityViewChange`. When a caller passes it, the toggle appears above the schedule. The existing `availabilityView` prop stays the only record of which mode is active; the component keeps no state of its own. The existing grid-or-text rendering, the text-field `<Schedule>` and the grid field are untouched.
- **`apps/web/modules/availability/[schedule]/schedule-view.tsx`** (+4): uses the hook and passes the mode and change handler to `AvailabilitySettings`.
- **`packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`** (+2): adds `"visual"` and `"availability_input_mode"`. The `"text"` key already existed.

## Other callers
`AvailabilitySettingsPlatformWrapper` passes neither prop, so it still shows the text view with no toggle, exactly as before. These are the only two callers. Nothing related to #72 changed: no sync or save logic was touched.

## Checks
- **Tests:** all `packages/features/schedules` tests pass: 251 passed, 4 skipped, including the 12 new ones.
- **TypeScript:** running `tsc --noEmit` on `apps/web` gives 0 errors.
- **Full `yarn type-check:ci --force`:** fails in `ui`, `app-store`, `embed-core` and `embed-snippet`. The reason is `tsc-absolute` / `tsc` not being found in this Windows shell (`command not found: tsc-absolute`, `spawn tsc ENOENT`). None of those packages import the new files. It's worth one full run in CI or WSL before you merge.
- **Biome:** no errors or warnings in the new files, only the same minor "nursery" notes the existing grid files already get. In the two edited files, no lint issue falls on a changed line. Biome also reports formatting changes on every line, but those are Windows line endings (CRLF) from `core.autocrlf=true`, not real changes.

## Remaining limitations
1. **`AvailabilitySettings` itself has no automated test.** The repo's tests don't cover `packages/platform` at all. The "one view at a time" test uses a small stand-in component with the same either/or logic, not the real settings page.
2. **Users who saved Visual will see Text for a split second** after a full page load before the grid appears. That's the price of avoiding the hydration mismatch.
3. **The toggle is imported from `@calcom/ui/components/form`,** which looks like a barrel import. It's the deepest path the `ui` package allows, and the file already imports from it.
4. **The choice applies per tab, not per schedule.** It's one setting for the browser tab, shared by all schedules, and cleared when the tab closes, as the issue specifies.
5. **Not tested in a real browser.** I didn't run the app to try it by hand. Clicking through `/availability/<id>` is worth doing.

<pasted_content id="3c58">
I've completed manual testing for Issue #71 (Add Toggle to Switch Between Text-Field and Calendar Grid Modes) on my local cal.diy website using Google Chrome on Windows.

Before I commit my changes, I want you to perform a thorough final code review, investigate the issue I found, and verify that the implementation fully satisfies Issue #71.

## Manual Testing Results

The following tests passed:

1. **Toggle visibility:** The Text / Visual toggle appears on the availability settings page.
2. **Mode switching:** Clicking Visual displays the calendar grid, and clicking Text displays the original text-field editor. Only one mode appears at a time.
3. **Visual persistence after refresh:** Selecting Visual and refreshing keeps Visual selected.
4. **Persistence after navigation:** Selecting Visual, navigating to another section, and returning to Availability preserves Visual mode.
5. **Text persistence after refresh:** Selecting Text and refreshing keeps Text selected.
6. **Keyboard accessibility:** Using the Right Arrow and Enter keys switches from Text to Visual.
7. **Reverse keyboard navigation:** Using the Left Arrow and Enter keys switches from Visual back to Text.
8. **Text re-click:** Clicking Text repeatedly does not deselect it or hide the editor.
9. **Persistence across schedules:** Selecting Visual and opening a different availability schedule preserves Visual mode.
10. **Visual re-click:** Clicking Visual repeatedly keeps the calendar grid visible.
11. **Existing Text editor:** The original text-field editor still allows editing availability times.
12. **Unsaved changes:** Changing a time without saving and refreshing restores the original saved value.
13. **Session isolation:** Opening the availability page in a separate, independently opened browser tab starts in Text mode.

## Issue Found During Manual Testing

**Brief Text-mode flash when refreshing in Visual mode**

When Visual is selected and I refresh the page, the Text editor briefly appears before the Visual calendar grid loads.

You previously mentioned this as a limitation caused by initializing the mode as Text to avoid Next.js hydration mismatches.

Please investigate whether this can be improved without introducing hydration issues, unnecessary complexity, or changes outside Issue #71.

If the safest solution is to keep the current behavior, explain why and document it as a known limitation. Do not introduce a complicated workaround for a minor visual issue.

## Final Code Review Requirements

Please:

1. Compare the implementation directly against every acceptance criterion in Issue #71.
2. Confirm the existing text-field UI remains unmodified.
3. Confirm only one input mode is rendered at a time.
4. Verify that sessionStorage persistence works correctly and handles unavailable storage safely.
5. Review state ownership and ensure there are no conflicting sources of truth.
6. Review accessibility, including keyboard navigation, labels, focus indicators, and selected states.

```text
import { createRouterCaller } from "app/_trpc/context";
import type { PageProps } from "app/_types";
import { _generateMetadata } from "app/_utils";
import { notFound } from "next/navigation";
import { z } from "zod";

import { availabilityRouter } from "@calcom/trpc/server/routers/viewer/availability/_router";
import { travelSchedulesRouter } from "@calcom/trpc/server/routers/viewer/travelSchedules/_router";

import { AvailabilitySettingsWebWrapper } from "~/availability/[schedule]/schedule-view";

const querySchema = z.object({
  schedule: z
    .string()
    .refine((val) => !isNaN(Number(val)), {
      message: "schedule must be a string that can be cast to a number",
    })
    .transform((val) => Number(val)),
});

export const generateMetadata = async () => {
  return await _generateMetadata(
    (t) => t("availability"),
    () => "",
    undefined,
    undefined,
    "/availability"
  );
};

const Page = async ({ params }: PageProps) => {
  const parsed = querySchema.safeParse(await params);
  if (!parsed.success) {
    notFound();
  }
  const scheduleId = parsed.data.schedule;

  const [availabilityCaller, travelSchedulesCaller] = await Promise.all([
    createRouterCaller(availabilityRouter),
    createRouterCaller(travelSchedulesRouter),
  ]);

  const [scheduleData, travelSchedulesData] = await Promise.all([
    availabilityCaller.schedule.get({ scheduleId }),
    travelSchedulesCaller.get(),
  ]);

  if (!scheduleData) {
    notFound();
  }

  return (
    <AvailabilitySettingsWebWrapper scheduleData={scheduleData} travelSchedulesData={travelSchedulesData} />
  );
};

export default Page;
```

```typescript
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { AvailabilitySettings } from "@calcom/atoms/availability/AvailabilitySettings";
import {
  AVAILABILITY_VIEW_STORAGE_KEY,
  useAvailabilityView,
} from "@calcom/features/schedules/hooks/useAvailabilityView";

// The web shell, text editor and timezone select pull in tRPC and session providers that are
// irrelevant to which input mode is shown, so they are replaced with lightweight stand-ins
vi.mock("@calcom/web/modules/shell/Shell", () => ({
  default: ({ heading, children }: { heading?: ReactNode; children?: ReactNode }) => (
    <div>
      {heading}
      {children}
    </div>
  ),
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/web/modules/schedules/components/Schedule", () => ({
  default: () => <div data-testid="text-field-schedule" />,
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/web/modules/timezone/components/TimezoneSelect", () => ({
  TimezoneSelect: () => <div data-testid="timezone-select" />,
}));

const schedule = {
  name: "Working hours",
  id: 1,
  isLastSchedule: false,
  isDefault: true,
  workingHours: [],
  dateOverrides: [],
  timeZone: "UTC",
  availability: Array.from({ length: 7 }, () => []),
  schedule: [],
};

const baseProps = {
  schedule,
  handleDelete: vi.fn(),
  handleSubmit: vi.fn(),
  isDeleting: false,
  isSaving: false,
  isLoading: false,
  timeFormat: 12,
  weekStart: "Sunday",
  backPath: "/availability",
};

// Wires the real hook to the real component the same way the web schedule page does
function WebAvailabilitySettings() {
  const [availabilityView, setAvailabilityView] = useAvailabilityView();

  return (
    <AvailabilitySettings
      {...baseProps}
      availabilityView={availabilityView}
      onAvailabilityViewChange={setAvailabilityView}
    />
  );
}

const textEditor = () => screen.queryByTestId("text-field-schedule");
const visualGrid = () => screen.queryByRole("grid");

describe("AvailabilitySettings Text / Visual toggle", () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    window.sessionStorage.clear();
  });

  it("does not render the toggle when no change handler is passed", () => {
    render(<AvailabilitySettings {...baseProps} />);

    expect(screen.queryByTestId("availability-view-visual")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(textEditor()).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(visualGrid()).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("switches between the text editor and the visual grid, rendering only one", async () => {
    render(<WebAvailabilitySettings />);

    expect(textEditor()).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(visualGrid()).not.toBeInTheDocument();

    await userEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("availability-view-visual"));
    expect(visualGrid()).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(textEditor()).not.toBeInTheDocument();

    await userEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("availability-view-text"));
    expect(textEditor()).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(visualGrid()).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("restores the visual grid from sessionStorage on mount", async () => {
    window.sessionStorage.setItem(AVAILABILITY_VIEW_STORAGE_KEY, "grid");

    render(<WebAvailabilitySettings />);

    expect(await screen.findByRole("grid")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(textEditor()).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByTestId("availability-view-visual")).toHaveAttribute("aria-checked", "true");
  });
});
```

I found no bugs in the Issue #71 code, and it's ready for you to commit. The one problem was in my new test file, which Biome flagged and I fixed. Two things to watch when you stage: leave out `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` and `QUIZ-STUDY-NOTES.md`, and make sure the full type check passes in CI, since it can't run on this Windows setup.

## The Text-mode flash
**I recommend keeping the current behavior.** This page is rendered on the server, and the server can't read `sessionStorage`, so the first HTML your browser shows is always Text mode. The browser only learns you picked Visual once the page's JavaScript loads. No client-side change can remove that window. The options I looked at:

| Option | Why I rejected it |
|---|---|
| Read storage earlier (`useLayoutEffect` / `useSyncExternalStore`) | Saves at most one frame, because the server's Text HTML is already on screen while JavaScript loads. On React 18.2, `useLayoutEffect` also logs a warning during server rendering. |
| Hide the editor until the page has loaded | Replaces the flash with a blank area for every user, including Text users. Worse. |
| Store the choice in a cookie the server can read | Would remove the flash, but changes behavior: a cookie is shared across tabs, so your test 13 would fail. It also means changing the server page, which is outside #71. |

I added one line to the comment in `useAvailabilityView.ts` explaining why the flash happens, so the next person doesn't try to "fix" it.

## Review against Issue #71
| Requirement | Result |
|---|---|
| Clearly labeled Text / Visual toggle on the availability page | ✅ Uses the existing `ToggleGroup`, labeled "Availability input mode" for screen readers. |
| Only one mode shown at a time | ✅ Uses #69's existing either/or rendering. Now covered by a test on the real component. |
| Choice persists within the session | ✅ Stored in `sessionStorage`. Survives refresh, navigation and switching schedules. A new tab starts on Text. |
| Existing text-field UI unchanged | ✅ The diff never touches `<Schedule>`, `ScheduleComponent` or the web `Schedule` component. |
| #72 (data sync) stays out of scope | ✅ No change to the form, save or grid sync code. |

- **Storage safety:** every read and write goes through `@calcom/lib/webstorage`, which catches errors. Unknown stored values are ignored. If storage throws, the toggle still works and simply doesn't remember the choice. All of this is tested.
- **State ownership:** there's one source of truth. The page owns the mode through the hook, and `AvailabilitySettings` only receives `availabilityView` and reports changes through `onAvailabilityViewChange`. It keeps no copy of its own.
- **Accessibility:** the group has a label, each option's selected state is announced, and Tab, arrow keys and Space/Enter all work (tested, and matches your manual tests 6–7). One caveat: the shared `ToggleGroup` has no custom focus ring, so it relies on Chrome's default focus outline. Every other `ToggleGroup` in the app works the same way, and I didn't change the shared component.
- **Other callers:** `AvailabilitySettingsPlatformWrapper` (used by the platform example app through `@calcom/atoms`) passes neither prop. It keeps the old behavior of Text mode with no toggle. A test now checks this.

## Changes made in this round
1. **New integration test:** `apps/web/modules/availability/[schedule]/AvailabilitySettings.view-toggle.test.tsx` renders the **real** `AvailabilitySettings` wired to the real hook, the same way `schedule-view.tsx` does. Only the web shell, the text editor and the timezone picker are stubbed. It checks three things: no toggle when no handler is passed, switching shows one view at a time, and a saved Visual choice is restored. It lives in `apps/web` because the repo's test setup doesn't run tests under `packages/platform`. To confirm it can catch bugs, I temporarily broke the grid/text branch: 2 of 3 tests failed. I then restored the file and confirmed its diff matched the original.
2. **Import order fix:** Biome flagged the new test file's import order as an error; I applied its automatic fix to that file only.
3. **Comment:** added the one line about the flash, described above.
